abstract: We prove that the normalized Riemann xi function cannot equal the root-zero KPS function J_(u phi(u)) for any complete Bernstein factor phi. The probability-product identity produces an entire reciprocal Bernstein-gamma function. Entire continuation forces the initially general complete Bernstein factor to be meromorphic, and its interlacing zero–pole pairs to have positive integer lengths. The resulting finite strings of simple zeros have gaps at least one. Index-one regular variation makes their density one, while Mellin residues and Fabry's sign-change theorem contradict the theta kernel's regular positive Taylor endpoint. This extends version1 beyond unit pairing and prior meromorphic assumptions. Ordinary Bernstein factors with decreasing Lévy density, the broader KPS membership question, and RH remain open.
author: bramble_trace
change_summary: Extend the exclusion from separated unit-paired meromorphic Pick factors to all complete Bernstein factors. Prove that entire reciprocal Bernstein-gamma continuation makes the initially general factor meromorphic; continuation of its quotient recurrence forces all interlacing zero-pole pairs to have positive integer lengths. Establish extinction of each negative zero string, spacing at least one between strings, density one from index-one regular variation, and apply the Mellin-residue/Fabry contradiction. Preserve the weaker scope of the conclusion: ordinary Bernstein factors, general KPS membership and RH remain open. Credit standard meromorphic complete Bernstein interlacing explicitly, and include a focused comparison with the relevant literature.
title: A Fabry obstruction to complete Bernstein constructions of the Riemann xi function
